claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have a child, Alex, who's 10 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'll help you determine if you're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

To start, can you tell me: Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask about your relationship to Alex.

Are you Alex's parent, or do you have another relationship to him (such as being a guardian, foster carer, or someone else who is responsible for him)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm Alex's parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand Alex's living arrangements.

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand the situation better.

Can you tell me who Alex lives with, and do you contribute to the cost of supporting Alex (for example, by paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upbringing)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his other parent. I do contribute towards his upkeep - I help out with things like clothes and bits and pieces for school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine eligibility, I need to understand the amount you're contributing.

The current Child Benefit rate for an eldest or only child is £25.60 per week. Are you contributing at least this amount (£25.60 per week or approximately £110 per month) towards Alex's costs for things like clothes, school items, and other expenses?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not contributing that much. I give about £20 a week to help out with his things.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment.

Is Alex's other parent (the one he lives with) currently claiming Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if they are or not, to be honest.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay. Let me ask a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Is Alex in full-time non-advanced education or approved training? (At 10 years old, I assume he's in primary school, but I want to confirm he's in education.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in school - primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to make sure I have all the information:

1. Are you currently receiving any other benefits or support for Alex from the government?

2. Is there any reason why Alex might be considered to be in your care or primarily your responsibility (for example, does he stay with you regularly, or are there any court orders or formal arrangements in place)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any other benefits or support for Alex. And no, there aren't any court orders or formal arrangements - he just lives with his other parent full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: While you are Alex's parent and live in the UK, Alex doesn't live with you - he lives full-time with his other parent. In situations where a child doesn't live with you, you can still claim Child Benefit if you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit rate towards supporting that child. 

The current Child Benefit rate for an eldest or only child is £25.60 per week. You mentioned that you contribute about £20 per week towards Alex's costs for things like clothes and school items. Unfortunately, this falls short of the required £25.60 per week threshold.

Additionally, since Alex lives with his other parent, they would have the primary claim to Child Benefit for him.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if Alex comes to live with you, or if you increase your financial contributions to at least £25.60 per week - you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
